sanitizedFindings.label: BMM-M-01
sanitizedFindings.title: Migration silently bricks the mint-sell-donate funder: its hardcoded BATCH_MINTER constant still points at the retired old minter
sanitizedFindings.description: mint-sell-donate is the ongoing operational funder that tops up the BatchNFTMinter USDC pot (mint phUSD -> sUSDS -> USDS -> USDC via PSM buyGem). Its donation target `address constant BATCH_MINTER = 0x6e98...5071` (the OLD minter) is a compile-time constant with NO env override. It self-checks `require(IPoolerCfg(LIVE_POOLER).batchMinter() == BATCH_MINTER, "batchMinter != live pooler")` at line 308. This migration repoints `POOLER.batchMinter()` to the NEW minter. Consequently, the very next mint-sell-donate run reverts at line 308 before any funds move.
sanitizedFindings.impact: Fail-SAFE, not fail-dangerous: the require aborts the run, so USDC is NEVER donated into the dead old contract (no stranded funds). BUT the protocol's only documented pot-refill path is rendered inoperable until someone edits the source constant, recompiles, and re-runs. The new minter's nudge pot stops being topped up beyond the one-time 128.57 USDC seed + per-mint donate-forward, degrading the nudge incentive over time. The migration ships no accompanying patch to this sibling and the closure has no automated linkage between them.
sanitizedFindings.evidence: side-effects.json clusterChecks[0]; grep confirms BATCH_MINTER is `constant` at line 279 (not vm.envOr); preview trace shows POOLER.setBatchMinter(new) + post-flight pooler.batchMinter == new minter; mint-sell-donate line 308 asserts equality against the stale OLD constant.
sanitizedFindings.recommendation: Either (a) make mint-sell-donate's BATCH_MINTER env/config-driven (read from live pooler.batchMinter() and assert it has code) so it tracks migrations automatically, or (b) include a source-bump of MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter.s.sol (BATCH_MINTER -> new minter) as an explicit post-migration checklist/cluster step. Document the ordering dependency in the Story 057 plan.

sanitizedFindings.label: BMM-L-01
sanitizedFindings.title: MigrateBatchNFTMinter lacks a chainid guard, unlike its sibling funder
sanitizedFindings.description: run() has no `require(block.chainid == 1)`; it relies solely on --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET and hardcoded mainnet address constants. The sibling MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter pins chainid (line 289), so this is an inconsistency in the same cluster. A misconfigured RPC env or a fat-fingered --fork-url would let the broadcast path execute against the wrong chain.
sanitizedFindings.impact: Low: a broadcast against a non-mainnet chain would mostly revert on the first external call to a non-existent contract, and the broadcast requires a Ledger signature. But it removes a cheap, standard fail-fast guard the rest of the cluster relies on, and the repo CLAUDE.md Configuration-Safety section mandates an explicit network guard for real-network scripts.
sanitizedFindings.evidence: intent.md access section; script lines 114-140 contain no chainid check; sibling MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter.s.sol:289 `require(block.chainid == 1, ...)`.
sanitizedFindings.recommendation: Add `require(block.chainid == 1, "expected mainnet (1)")` at the top of run() (or gate behind PREVIEW for local), matching the sibling and the repo's Configuration-Safety gate.
